title: KV halo-slice merging and dynamic placement for multi-GPU tensor-pipeline KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies the KV cache is often sliced across GPUs in ways that create small, overlapping ‘halo’ regions of keys. These halo regions cause excessive duplication, fragmentation, and unnecessary cross-GPU requests during continuous batching and KV prefetching. That increases tail latency and reduces effective KV residency, driving higher spill rates and token cost.

Goal: Implement a 'halo-slice merging' allocator and dynamic placement policy that: (1) coalesces adjacent KV slices across pipeline boundaries when beneficial, (2) places merged slices onto the minimal set of GPUs using a cost function aware of tensor-parallel replica layout and active batch length distributions, and (3) integrates with continuous batching and prefetch controllers to reduce cross-device synchronization.

Key ideas:
- Identify halo regions created by pipeline-stage boundaries and small-slice splits that historically result from fixed slab-sizes.
- Merge neighboring halos opportunistically at allocation time when merging reduces total replicated bytes by >X% or predicted cross-GPU fetches by >Y.
- Use a dynamic placement cost function: cost = alpha * estimated_cross_gpu_fetches + beta * memory_imbalance_penalty + gamma * eviction_risk. Tune alpha/beta/gamma per topology.
- Provide a fallback replicated mode for very low-latency single-token workloads where replication is cheaper than cross-device fetches.
- Expose placement hints to the continuous-batcher and KV-prefetcher so they can schedule requests against the GPUs holding merged slices, reducing blocking waits.

Acceptance criteria:
- 20–40% reduction in cross-GPU KV fetches on representative pipeline+tensor workloads (internal perf suite).
- Maintain or improve 95th-percentile generation latency for batch sizes 1–16.
- No increase in memory OOM events on standard clusters; spill rate reduced by at least 10% for target workloads.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: global model sharding changes, new quantization formats, and hardware-level page migration primitives.

Design artifacts: confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/KV+Halo+Slice+Merging (design + cost model), perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/kv-halo-experiments, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289
comments: 2026-03-10: Aisha - initial writeup + proposal. Identified that many small workloads suffering from fragmentation are 50% costlier due to duplicated halos.
2026-03-11: Marco - added placement cost function draft; suggested alpha=1.5, beta=0.8, gamma=2.0 as starting point. Noted interaction with existing KV slab allocator and continuous batcher API.

2026-03-12: Design review (ENG/Research): consensus to prefer opportunistic merging on allocation rather than background compaction to avoid extra runtime copies. Research suggested adding an eviction-reserve to merged slices to reduce thrashing.
2026-03-12: UX/Debug note - adding a placement trace tag so Console can show which GPU holds merged halos for a request; added to rollout checklist.

2026-03-13: Marco - prototyped merging in allocator; local bench shows 28% fewer cross-device fetches on small-chat workloads with 4 pipeline stages. Need to validate at scale (8+ GPUs) and with heterogeneous device sizes.
2026-03-13: PR feedback from Lina (SRE) - ensure merged placements respect node-level isolation in Dedicated mode; added 'respect_isolation' flag in planner.
2026-03-13: TODO: add regression tests for continuous-batcher pinning logic, and add telemetry for 'merged vs replicated' counters per topology in Console.
implementation_notes: Allocator changes live in allocator/halo_merger.{cc,h}. The placement planner integrates with the existing tp-aware placement API; added a Planner::scorePlacement() call. Continuous-batcher now supports optional 'preferred_gpu' hints returned by KV::getPlacement(key-range). Added metrics: kv.halo.merged_count, kv.halo.merged_bytes, kv.halo.cross_fetch_reduction.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for merger correctness and no key-loss (allocator unit test suite). 2) Synthetic perf runs: small-chat, doc-summarization, and long-context streaming with batch sizes 1/4/8. 3) Large-scale integration run on 8x A100 cluster to validate memory balance and spill behavior. 4) Canary rollout with Dedicated customers on non-production capacity. 5) Telemetry dashboard checks for merged_count and 95p latency regressions.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Feature-flagged in runtime-1.24 on internal clusters. Stage 2: Canary on 2 dedicated customers with opt-in toggles and extended telemetry. Stage 3: Default enabled for 4+ GPU topologies if perf targets met.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Merged placement may increase memory imbalance and cause OOM on tightly packed clusters. Mitigation: memory_imbalance_penalty in cost function and hard cap preventing placement if imbalance exceeds 8% per node. Risk: Added complexity in continuous-batcher may cause scheduling stalls. Mitigation: expose hint as a best-effort optimization; batcher falls back to round-robin when hint unavailable.
